text:
maria: Quick design thread — proposal to call the new automatic fallback UX the 'switchboard' so operators can route failures/quality degradations into named lanes (fast, safe, degraded-slim). Thoughts?

aj: Nice metaphor. Helps mental model. Main question: do lanes map to concrete model variants (e.g., quantized small) or to behavior policies (rate-limit, shorter responses)?

maria: Ideally both — lane has a tiered policy bundle: model_variant + degrade_strategy + quota-adjustments. So selecting lane applies all 3.

kevin: Agree with bundling. UX needs to surface what each lane changes to avoid surprises. I worry about hidden token-cost changes. Maybe show delta estimates?

sasha: Delta estimates would be huge for product trust. Can we compute expected token and latency delta from rollout sim data? We already have sim runs for canaries.

ellie: +1 on sim. Also need a clear operator override: 'sticky' lane for a route until a human clears. Avoids flapping during incidents.

aj: UX nit: don't force lanes to be exclusive. Allow fallback chain (primary -> lane A -> lane B). The switchboard should show chain with probabilities and triggers.

maria: Good call. Chain view with weights. Also triggers: errors (5xx), latency p95, or quality drop (eval mismatch). Want to let users pick triggers and hysteresis.

kevin: Can we show a quick policy snippet inline? Something like:

```
{ "lane": "degraded-slim", "model": "gpt-small-q8", "triggers": [{"type": "p95", "threshold_ms": 800}], "max_share": 0.2 }
```

maria: Exactly. UX should let you edit that JSON or use form controls. But editing raw JSON should show validation and a preview of audit annotations.

ops-bot: [auto] When a lane is created it will generate an audit record: id=lane-20260321-782, policy_hash=sha256:abcd...

ellie: Audit records should include sim snapshot and last 24h telemetry sample used for decision. Otherwise ops get blindfolded.

sasha: Question about telemetry surface: show a sparkline for each signal (p50/p95/errors/quality) and a 'confidence' badge computed from sample size.

aj: For quotas: lane-level token cap vs global per-route cap — we should clarify precedence. I propose precedence: operator override > lane-cap > global-cap. Document in UI tooltip.

kevin: Also need to call out interactions with rate-limit mesh: if upstream rate-limit kills requests, lane won't trigger by p95 alone. Include a 'signal origin' label (client-side/infra) in trigger history.

maria: UX tasks: 1) chain visual + lane inspector 2) sim-run button with delta estimates 3) create audit record with sim snapshot 4) sticky override toggle 5) tooltips for precedence. I'll sketch flows.

ellie: I'll attach runbook snippets for sticky overrides and a check-list for post-rollback verification.

sasha: Quick API debate: Should the internal policy API accept lane bundles as compact objects or fully normalized refs? Compact is nicer for UI but normalized refs are easier for rollout engine.

aj: We can accept both: UI posts compact payload, server normalizes and returns canonical ref. Keep canonical in audit.

kevin: UX detail: in rollout history, show the canonical ref plus the original compact payload so reviewers can see intent vs actual config.

maria: Love it. One last thing — naming: avoid 'fallback' for the public UI (confuses people). 'Switchboard' or 'contingency lanes' preferred.

ops-bot: [auto] Created ticket: ENG-UX-6212 "Switchboard lane inspector mockups" assigned to maria.

maria: Thanks — I'll post mocks tomorrow and tag infra for API acceptance criteria. :thumbsup:
